newsitem.title: UK: Charles and Diana reunited for son's confirmation.
newsitem.headline: Charles and Diana reunited for son's confirmation.

text.p: Britain's Prince Charles and his former wife Princess Diana were briefly reunited on Sunday for the confirmation of their oldest son, Prince William.

The couple, who divorced last August after wrangling for months over a settlement, joined Queen Elizabeth and other members of the royal family for a Mother's Day lunch at Windsor Castle before the afternoon ceremony.
Thousands of spectators gathered outside the gates of the castle west of London as the couple and their sons William and Harry arrived in a rare public appearance together.
About 40 guests, including the Queen Mother and 14-year-old William's godparents, attended the ceremony, which marks his full membership and acceptance of the teaching of Anglican Church.

In a break with tradition, Bishop of London Richard Chartres conducted the confirmation instead of the Archbishop of Canterbury, the head of the Anglican Church, who usually performs the ceremony for members of the royal family.
Charles, an admirer of Chartres, chose him specially for the occasion.

Charles' assistant, Tiggy Legge-Bourke, who has acted as a companion and surrogate mother to the young princes, did not attend. Press reports said she was barred by Diana who resented her closeness to them.
